# ui::Property

Header: `winui/core/Property.hpp`.

```cpp
template <typename T> class Property
```

Derives from `ui::PropertyBase`.

An observable value: application state written once, from which every display of it is derived through [bind()](namespace-ui.md#bind) or [observe()](#observe).

T must be equality comparable, because the equality gate is not optional: [set()](#set) compares before it assigns, so a no-op write notifies nobody and a dependency cycle terminates instead of recursing. Non-copyable and non-movable, since bindings hold a reference to it. A Property may outlive the controls bound to it or be destroyed first, which ends the bindings. UI thread only: [set()](#set) is not synchronized.

Example: 
```cpp
ui::Property<int> clicks{0};

window.set_content(ui::VerticalStack{
    .spacing  = 12,
    .content  = {
        ui::Text{.text = ui::bind(clicks, [](int n) { return std::format("Clicks: {}", n); })},
        ui::Button{.text = "Click me", .on_click = [&] { ++clicks; }},
        ui::Button{.text = "Reset", .on_click = [&] { clicks = 0; }},
    },
});
```

## value_type

```cpp
using ui::Property< T >::value_type = T
```

The stored type.

## Property

```cpp
Property() = default
```

Holds a value-initialized T.

## Property

```cpp
Property(T value)
```

Holds `value`; no observer exists yet, so nothing is notified.

## get

```cpp
const T& get() const noexcept
```

The current value. The reference is invalidated by the next [set()](#set).

## operator*

```cpp
const T& operator*() const noexcept
```

Same as [get()](#get).

## operator->

```cpp
const T* operator->() const noexcept
```

Member access to the current value, e.g. `title->size()`.

## set

```cpp
void set(T value, std::source_location where = std::source_location::current())
```

Assign and, if the value changed (`!=` by T's operator==), notify every observer synchronously before returning. UI thread only: a build with thread checks reports a write from another thread than the property's first notifying one, naming `where` (the caller's file and line; leave it defaulted).

## operator=

```cpp
Property& operator=(detail::AssignedValue<T> value)
```

Same as [set()](#set): `clicks = 0;`, and a thread check report names the caller's line as [set()](#set)'s does. A braced value of several parts goes through [set()](#set): `size.set({4, 3});`.

## operator+=

```cpp
Property& operator+=(detail::AssignedValue<T> delta)
    requires (!std::same_as<T, bool>) && requires(const T& a, const T& b) { { a + b } -> std::convertible_to<T>; }
```

Adds `delta` through [set()](#set), so the equality gate applies: `count += 5;`, `log += "Saved\n";`. Exists when `T + T` gives a T, except for bool.

## operator-=

```cpp
Property& operator-=(detail::AssignedValue<T> delta)
    requires (!std::same_as<T, bool>) && requires(const T& a, const T& b) { { a - b } -> std::convertible_to<T>; }
```

Subtracts `delta` through [set()](#set): `remaining -= 1;`. Exists when `T - T` gives a T, except for bool.

## operator++

```cpp
Property& operator++()
    requires requires(T& t) { ++t; }
```

Adds one through [set()](#set): `++clicks;`. Exists when T has a `++`.

## operator--

```cpp
Property& operator--()
    requires requires(T& t) { --t; }
```

Subtracts one through [set()](#set): `--remaining;`. Exists when T has a `--`.

## operator++

```cpp
T operator++(int)
    requires requires(T& t) { ++t; }
```

As `++clicks`, returning the value from before, as `++` on the T itself would.

## operator--

```cpp
T operator--(int)
    requires requires(T& t) { --t; }
```

As `--remaining`, returning the value from before.

## toggle

```cpp
void toggle(std::source_location where = std::source_location::current())
    requires std::same_as<T, bool>
```

Flips a `Property<bool>` through [set()](#set): `dark_mode.toggle();`.

## update

```cpp
template <typename Fn>
void update(Fn&& fn, std::source_location where = std::source_location::current())
    requires std::invocable<Fn&, T&>
```

Read-modify-write for values that are awkward to rebuild by hand (a container, a struct with several fields). `fn` mutates a copy; the equality gate then decides whether anything is notified, so a mutation that changes nothing still costs nothing. `where` is for the thread check, as in [set()](#set).

## observe

```cpp
Subscription observe(Callback<void(const T&)> fn) const
```

Observe changes. The returned [Subscription](subscription.md) must be kept alive for `fn` to keep firing; store it on the [Element](../tree/element.md) that depends on it ([Element::add_subscription](../tree/element.md#add_subscription)) so subscription lifetime is node lifetime. Observers are called newest subscription first. `fn` is not called for the current value. A caller that wants the initial value reads [get()](#get), as [Binding<T>](binding.md) does.
